denny_001_instruction: Can you help little Denny find his way to Mommy Coral? Use your finger to draw a path through the maze so Denny can reach his mama on the Sandy Shore.
denny_001_answer: Sandy beaches are home to many animals! Seagulls, hermit crabs, sandpipers, and tiny sand crabs all love the shore. At low tide you can also find sea anemones and small fish hiding in tide pools.
denny_001_completion: Denny found Mommy Coral and they can spend the day together on the Sandy Shore.
denny_002_instruction: A giant shell path winds through the coral garden. Help Denny avoid every jellyfish and trace the safe path to Finn.
denny_002_answer: Jellyfish do not have bones or brains. Their soft bodies drift with the currents, and many jellyfish use stinging tentacles to protect themselves.
denny_002_completion: Denny traced the shell path perfectly and slipped past every jellyfish to reach Finn. Finn cheered at the end of the shell garden.
denny_003_instruction: Can you help Denny swim through the lagoon to find his little sister Sandy? Draw a line with your finger to show Denny the way through the bubbles.
denny_003_answer: Lagoons are calm and sheltered, so many sea creatures love them! Sea turtles, sea horses, small colourful fish, and spotted rays often make their home in warm lagoon waters.
denny_003_completion: Hooray! Denny found Sandy and now they can play with the bubbles together.
denny_004_instruction: Can you help Denny get to Daddy Reef? Draw a gentle line with your finger to show Denny the way through the maze so he can share his beautiful shell.
denny_004_answer: Baby crabs like Denny love to explore tide pools where they can find shells, small fish, and colorful sea anemones.
denny_004_completion: Denny reached Daddy Reef and they looked at the pretty shell together.
denny_005_instruction: Can you help Denny reach Stella by drawing a line through the maze? Take your time and guide Denny safely to his wise friend.
denny_005_answer: Some sea creatures like jellyfish and plankton can make their own light to glow in the dark ocean.
denny_005_completion: Denny made it to Stella and learned that tiny sea creatures make the rocks glow!
denny_006_instruction: Can you help Denny find his shy friend Bubbles? Draw a gentle line through the coral garden to bring these ocean friends together.
denny_006_answer: Seahorses like Bubbles wrap their tails around coral to stay in one place while they rest.
denny_006_completion: Wonderful! Denny found Bubbles and now they can play together in the coral garden.
denny_007_instruction: Can you help Denny follow Shelly's bubble trail? Draw a gentle line with your finger to guide Denny through the swaying kelp forest to reach his friend Shelly.
denny_007_answer: Kelp forests are home to so much more than kelp! Sea otters, sea lions, rockfish, and spiny sea urchins all live there. The tall kelp fronds create a whole underwater jungle for animals to hide and hunt in.
denny_007_completion: Denny found Shelly in the peaceful kelp forest and now they can explore together.
denny_008_instruction: Can you help Denny find his way through the kelp forest to reach Ollie? Draw a gentle line with your finger to guide Denny safely to his octopus friend.
denny_008_answer: Besides kelp, many amazing creatures live in a kelp forest! Leopard sharks glide through the fronds, garibaldi fish glow bright orange, and sea otters wrap themselves in kelp to rest without drifting away.
denny_008_completion: Great job helping Denny reach Ollie in the kelp forest!
denny_009_instruction: Can you help Denny find his way through the shipwreck to reach his friend Finn? Draw a gentle line with your finger to guide Denny safely to where Finn is waiting by the treasure chest.
denny_009_answer: Real treasures have been found in shipwrecks! The Atocha wreck held gold coins, silver bars, and emeralds worth over 400 million dollars. Archaeologists carefully dive down to discover these hidden riches.
denny_009_completion: Great job helping Denny reach Finn at the shipwreck - now they can explore the treasure chest together!
denny_010_instruction: Can you help Denny find his way through the lagoon to reach Pearl? Draw a gentle line with your finger to show Denny the path to his friend.
denny_010_answer: Jellyfish like Pearl have been floating in the ocean for over 500 million years, even before dinosaurs lived on land.
denny_010_completion: Denny helped Pearl get untangled from the seaweed, and now they can swim together in the lagoon.
denny_011_instruction: Help Denny collect all the shells on the beach! Draw a path through the maze and pick up every shell before reaching Mommy Coral.
denny_011_answer: Seashells are the homes of soft-bodied animals called mollusks. When the animal grows too big, it makes a bigger shell!
denny_011_completion: Denny collected all the shells! Mommy Coral is so proud!
denny_012_instruction: Look at all those pearls! Help Denny explore the coral garden and collect every pearl before reaching Finn.
denny_012_answer: Pearls are made by oysters! When a tiny grain of sand gets inside, the oyster covers it with smooth layers until it becomes a pearl.
denny_012_completion: Denny found all the pearls! Finn is amazed!
denny_013_instruction: Sandy is making bubbles! Help Denny catch every bubble in the lagoon as you draw a path to reach Sandy.
denny_013_answer: Bubbles are round because the air inside pushes equally in all directions, making a sphere — the shape with the smallest surface!
denny_013_completion: Denny caught all of Sandy's bubbles! What fun!
denny_014_instruction: Sharp coral is covering the beach path. Help Denny avoid every coral branch and find the safe way to Daddy Reef.
denny_014_answer: Broken coral has very sharp edges that can cut skin easily. Coral also grows very slowly — some reefs add only about 2 centimetres each year! That is why it is so important to swim carefully and never touch or step on coral.
denny_014_completion: Denny slipped past every sharp coral branch and reached Daddy Reef safely. What a careful little explorer!
denny_015_instruction: Stella needs your help! Draw a path through the cove and collect all the lost stars before reaching Stella.
denny_015_answer: Starfish can regrow their arms if one breaks off! Some starfish have more than 5 arms — the sun star can have up to 40!
denny_015_completion: Denny found all of Stella's stars! She's so happy!
denny_016_instruction: Yummy clams everywhere! Help Denny find every clam hiding in the coral garden on the way to Bubbles.
denny_016_answer: Clams filter water to eat! A single clam can clean up to 50 gallons of water every day. That helps keep the ocean clean!
denny_016_completion: Denny found all the clams! Bubbles is ready for a feast!
denny_017_instruction: Seaweed is floating across the shortcut. Help Denny avoid the tangles and find the clear path to Shelly.
denny_017_answer: Seaweed is a superfood. It is used to make sushi wraps, ice cream, and even toothpaste. Kelp can grow up to 2 feet per day.
denny_017_completion: Denny dodged every swaying seaweed tangle and reached Shelly without getting stuck. Shelly gave a proud turtle grin.
denny_018_instruction: Ollie needs kelp for soup! Help Denny swim through the forest and collect every kelp leaf before reaching Ollie.
denny_018_answer: Kelp is a giant type of algae — not quite a plant, but it grows like one! It can reach 45 metres tall and creates whole underwater forests. Sea otters love kelp forests and wrap themselves in the fronds so they do not drift away while they sleep.
denny_018_completion: Denny gathered all the kelp! Ollie's soup will be delicious!
denny_019_instruction: Treasure hunt! Help Denny collect every sparkling gem hidden around the shipwreck before meeting Finn.
denny_019_answer: Real treasure has been found in shipwrecks! The Atocha shipwreck had gold and emeralds worth over 400 million dollars!
denny_019_completion: Denny found all the treasure! What an amazing adventure with Finn!
denny_020_instruction: Pufferfish are floating through the lagoon. Help Denny avoid every pufferfish and swim safely to Pearl.
denny_020_answer: Pufferfish puff up with water to look bigger when they are frightened. That helps warn other animals to stay back.
denny_020_completion: Denny swam safely past every pufferfish and reached Pearl at the end of the lagoon. Pearl cheered for his careful swimming!
denny_021_instruction: Blast off! Help Denny collect every guiding star on the launch pad before reaching Mommy Coral at the control room.
denny_021_answer: A rocket needs to travel at 40,000 kilometers per hour to escape Earth's gravity. That's fast enough to go around the world in less than an hour!
denny_021_completion: Denny launched into space! Mommy Coral is so proud!
denny_022_instruction: Bounce on the Moon! Help Denny pick up every moon rock in the crater before finding Daddy Reef.
denny_022_answer: The Moon has only one-sixth of Earth's gravity! If you weigh 30 kilograms on Earth, you'd weigh just 5 kilograms on the Moon.
denny_022_completion: Denny collected all the moon rocks! Daddy Reef is amazed by the bouncy adventure!
denny_023_instruction: Asteroid adventure! Help Denny collect every sparkling gem floating in the asteroid belt before finding Sandy.
denny_023_answer: Asteroids are space rocks left over from when our solar system formed 4.6 billion years ago! The asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter has millions of them.
denny_023_completion: Denny found Sandy and collected all the gems! What a rocky adventure!
denny_024_instruction: Alien planet! Help Denny gather every colorful alien flower in the glowing forest before reaching Finn.
denny_024_answer: Scientists have discovered over 5,000 planets outside our solar system! Some are in the 'habitable zone' where liquid water might exist.
denny_024_completion: Denny delivered the flowers to the aliens! Finn says they loved them!
denny_025_instruction: Zero gravity emergency! Help Denny collect every floating tool before finding Stella to fix the space station.
denny_025_answer: On the International Space Station, astronauts sleep in sleeping bags attached to the wall and eat food from pouches — otherwise it floats away!
denny_025_completion: Denny collected all the tools! Stella fixed the space station just in time!
denny_026_instruction: Drifting through the nebula! Help Denny collect every glowing spark in the colorful clouds before finding Ollie.
denny_026_answer: A nebula is a giant cloud of gas and dust in space where new stars are born! The Eagle Nebula has a famous region called 'Pillars of Creation' where stars are forming right now.
denny_026_completion: Denny collected all the stardust! Ollie's nebula painting is beautiful!
denny_027_instruction: Zooming on a comet! Help Denny pick up every glowing ice chunk in the comet's tail before reaching Shelly.
denny_027_answer: Comets are giant balls of ice and rock! As they get close to the Sun, the ice melts and creates a glowing tail that can stretch millions of kilometers.
denny_027_completion: Denny caught the comet and reached Shelly! What a wild space ride!
denny_028_instruction: Careful near the black hole! Help Denny collect every glowing light ring swirling around the edge before finding Bubbles.
denny_028_answer: A black hole has such powerful gravity that even light cannot escape! They form when a massive star collapses at the end of its life.
denny_028_completion: Denny collected all the light rings! Bubbles says the data is priceless — amazing science!
denny_029_instruction: Surfing Saturn's rings! Help Denny collect every shiny ice chunk in the rings before finding Pearl floating nearby.
denny_029_answer: Saturn's rings are made mostly of ice and rock, ranging from tiny grains to chunks as big as a house! The rings are incredibly thin — only about 10 meters thick in places.
denny_029_completion: Denny surfed all the way to Pearl through Saturn's rings! The most beautiful sight in the solar system!
denny_030_instruction: Stars everywhere! Help Denny collect every glowing constellation star in the starfield before meeting Finn at the center.
denny_030_answer: There are 88 officially named constellations! Ancient people used them as a map to navigate at sea and to track the seasons. Orion is one of the most famous.
denny_030_completion: Denny connected all the stars! Finn's constellation spells out D-E-N-N-Y!
denny_031_instruction: Welcome to Mars! Help Denny navigate the dusty red paths to reach Mommy Coral at the base camp.
denny_031_answer: Mars looks red because its soil is full of iron oxide — that's rust! Mars also has the tallest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons, three times taller than Mount Everest.
denny_031_completion: Denny explored Mars and found Mommy Coral! The first crab on Mars!
denny_032_instruction: Into the storm! Help Denny navigate through Jupiter's swirling cloud bands to find Daddy Reef in the eye of the storm.
denny_032_answer: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm that has been raging for over 350 years! It's so big that Earth could fit inside it. Jupiter is also the largest planet — 1,300 Earths could fit inside!
denny_032_completion: Denny flew through the storm! Daddy Reef has all the data they need!
denny_033_instruction: Base building time! Help Denny bounce across the winding Moon paths to reach Stella at the lunar base.
denny_033_answer: Scientists are working on plans for a real Moon base! People living there would need air, water, food, and protection from the Sun's radiation. They might even grow plants underground!
denny_033_completion: Denny arrived! Together, they finish building the lunar base!
denny_034_instruction: Amazing discovery! Help Denny follow the swirling energy paths to reach Ollie at the wormhole entrance.
denny_034_answer: A wormhole is a theoretical tunnel through space and time! Scientists think they might exist but have never found one. If they do exist, they could allow instant travel between distant parts of the universe.
denny_034_completion: Denny reached the portal! Denny and Ollie jump through the wormhole together!
denny_035_instruction: Glowing jungle! Help Denny find a path through the bioluminescent alien plants to reach Shelly.
denny_035_answer: Bioluminescence means making your own light! Fireflies, some jellyfish, anglerfish, and deep-sea creatures all glow. Some scientists think alien life might glow too!
denny_035_completion: Denny found Shelly! The alien jungle is the most beautiful place in the universe!
denny_036_instruction: Icy adventure! Help Denny navigate the slippery ice crystal paths across the frozen planet to reach Bubbles.
denny_036_answer: Neptune is the coldest planet at around -214°C — so cold that any water would freeze solid in an instant. It stays that cold because Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun and receives very little warmth.
denny_036_completion: Denny reached Bubbles! They slide together across the frozen sea!
denny_037_instruction: Race time! Help Denny rocket along the galactic race course to reach Sandy at the finish line!
denny_037_answer: The fastest spacecraft ever launched, the Parker Solar Probe, travels at 692,000 kilometres per hour — that is fast enough to fly from New York to Los Angeles in about 24 seconds!
denny_037_completion: Denny wins the space race! Sandy gives the winner's trophy — a shiny star!
denny_038_instruction: Mechanical world! Help Denny navigate the winding robot city paths to find Pearl.
denny_038_answer: There are robots on Mars right now! The Perseverance rover explores the Martian surface taking photos and collecting rock samples. It even has a tiny helicopter friend called Ingenuity!
denny_038_completion: Denny found Pearl! The friendly robots put on a light show to celebrate!
denny_039_instruction: Deep space mission! Help Denny navigate through the dense glowing star clouds to reach Finn at the galaxy core.
denny_039_answer: At the center of our Milky Way galaxy sits a supermassive black hole called Sagittarius A*. It's four million times heavier than our Sun! Thankfully, we're safely 26,000 light years away from it.
denny_039_completion: Denny reached the galaxy core! Together, they decode the mysterious signal!
denny_040_instruction: Heading home! Help Denny navigate through Earth's beautiful orbit to land safely and reach Mommy Coral.
denny_040_answer: The International Space Station orbits Earth 16 times every day! Astronauts who return from long missions have to learn to walk again because their muscles got weak in zero gravity.
denny_040_completion: Denny is home! Mommy Coral hugs Denny tight — the greatest space explorer in the world!
denny_041_instruction: Something is rustling in the bushes. Help Denny follow the path through the forest and find out who is making that noise.
denny_041_answer: Forests are full of sounds! Leaves rustling, branches creaking, animals scurrying — a healthy forest is never silent. Scientists can even tell how healthy a forest is by listening to it!
denny_041_completion: It was Maya. A tiny shy mouse peeked out from behind the bushes and smiled at Denny. So that was the little rustling sound all along.
denny_042_instruction: Maya knows a secret path! Help Denny follow Maya through the twisted forest trails to reach the magical mushroom clearing.
denny_042_answer: There are over 80 species of bioluminescent fungi — mushrooms that actually glow! They produce a soft green light at night. Scientists are still figuring out exactly why they do it.
denny_042_completion: Denny and Maya made it to the mushroom clearing! The giant glowing mushrooms light up all around them. Denny thinks the forest might be the most magical place he has ever visited.
denny_043_instruction: Bright flowers are blooming beside the brook. Help Denny collect every flower and bring them to Maya.
denny_043_answer: Flowers need sunlight, water, and healthy soil to grow. Near streams, the ground often stays damp enough to help many plants bloom.
denny_043_completion: Denny gathered every flower and brought them safely to Maya. The little bouquet looked beautiful beside the sparkling brook.
denny_044_instruction: Owls are sleeping on the path! Find a way around them to reach Maya at the other side.
denny_044_answer: Owls are nocturnal — they hunt at night because that is when many small animals like mice and voles are most active. Their huge eyes collect lots of light so they can see in the dark. Other nocturnal animals include bats, hedgehogs, and raccoons.
denny_044_completion: Denny tiptoed all the way through without waking a single owl! Maya claps quietly so she doesn't wake them either. What a clever little crab!
denny_045_instruction: Tiny fox tracks lead through the forest. Help Denny follow the right path to meet Finn the fox cub for the first time.
denny_045_answer: Animals leave many clues behind! Footprints in mud or snow, scratch marks on trees, and half-eaten leaves all show that an animal passed by. Foxes leave small oval paw prints with four toes — you might spot them near streams or soft soil.
denny_045_completion: Denny found Finn curled beside a hollow log. Finn's tail gave a happy little swish when he met Denny and Maya for the very first time.
denny_046_instruction: Blueberries are hiding all along the path. Help Denny collect every berry before reaching Finn.
denny_046_answer: Many forest animals eat berries, but some berries are only safe for animals. People should only eat berries when a grown-up knows they are safe.
denny_046_completion: Every blueberry made it safely to Finn. He shared the berry snack with Maya and Denny under the pine tree.
denny_047_instruction: The bees are busy near the honey tree. Help Denny find the safe path past them to Finn.
denny_047_answer: Bees help plants make seeds and fruit by moving pollen from flower to flower. That is called pollination.
denny_047_completion: Denny tiptoed safely past the bees. Finn cheered from the far side of the oak roots and showed Denny the way onward.
denny_048_instruction: Pip the frog is calling from the brook. Help Denny find the right path through the forest to meet Pip for the first time.
denny_048_answer: Frogs can breathe through their skin when it stays wet, which is one reason they like ponds and streams.
denny_048_completion: Denny found Pip beside the stepping stones. Pip gave one giant ribbit of welcome when he met Denny for the very first time.
denny_049_instruction: Smooth pebbles are scattered near the waterfall. Help Denny collect every pebble before reaching Pip.
denny_049_answer: Running water slowly rubs rough stones against each other and makes them smoother over time.
denny_049_completion: The pebbles made Pip's little splash pool sparkle. The waterfall mist felt cool and wonderful on Denny's shell.
denny_050_instruction: Some sleepy snakes are resting by the reeds. Help Denny find a careful path around them to Pip.
denny_050_answer: Snakes push against the ground with their scales and muscles to slither forward in smooth curves.
denny_050_completion: Denny glided around every sleepy snake. Pip clapped his little webbed feet from the lily pads.
denny_051_instruction: Birch the beaver is building near the stream. Help Denny find the best path through the maze to meet Birch for the first time.
denny_051_answer: Beaver dams can slow streams down and create ponds where lots of other animals can live.
denny_051_completion: Denny found Birch at the water's edge. Birch slapped the stream with his tail in a happy splashy hello when he met Denny for the first time.
denny_052_instruction: Branches are waiting along the path. Help Denny collect every stick before reaching Birch the beaver.
denny_052_answer: Beavers build dams to make calm ponds where they can build safe homes called lodges.
denny_052_completion: With every stick collected, Birch's new dam grew stronger. Denny felt like a real forest builder.
denny_053_instruction: The dog is asleep by the path. Help Denny find the safe way around without waking it.
denny_053_answer: Dogs have very strong noses and sharp hearing. Even while they rest, they notice interesting sounds and smells.
denny_053_completion: Denny slipped around the sleeping dog without a sound. Birch gave him a proud nod from the stream bank.
denny_054_instruction: Two long rabbit ears are peeking from the clover patch. Help Denny find the path to meet Clover the rabbit for the first time.
denny_054_answer: Rabbits like grassy areas because that is where their favourite food grows — grasses, clover, and leafy plants! Staying near low bushes and hedges also gives them quick hiding spots when a fox or hawk comes too close.
denny_054_completion: Denny reached the clover patch and met Clover at last. Clover twitched a tiny pink nose and gave Denny a bright, friendly hop of hello.
denny_055_instruction: Fresh clover leaves are scattered through the meadow. Help Denny collect every clover leaf before reaching Clover.
denny_055_answer: Wild rabbits like to eat grasses, clover, leaves, and tender plants they can find close to the ground.
denny_055_completion: Every clover leaf made Clover's lunch pile bigger. Clover gave Denny a happy hop and shared the shadiest spot in the meadow.
denny_056_instruction: Prickly thorn bushes are crowding the path. Help Denny find a careful way around them to reach Clover.
denny_056_answer: Thorns can protect plants by making hungry animals think twice before nibbling too much.
denny_056_completion: Denny slipped past every thorn bush without a scratch. Clover smiled and thumped one happy foot outside the burrow.
denny_057_instruction: Golden lights are blinking in the meadow. Help Denny find the winding path to meet Glow the firefly for the first time.
denny_057_answer: Fireflies glow to talk to one another. Each kind of firefly has its own special blinking pattern.
denny_057_completion: Denny reached Glow just as the meadow lit up like a tiny starry sky. It was the first time they met, and Maya gasped because the whole meadow looked so beautiful.
denny_058_instruction: Twinkling lights are floating all along the trail. Help Denny collect every glowing spark before reaching Glow.
denny_058_answer: Moonlight, fireflies, and even some mushrooms can make a forest glow at night in magical ways.
denny_058_completion: Every golden sparkle made the meadow brighter. Glow whirled around Denny in a happy ring of light.
denny_059_instruction: Shiny spider webs are stretched across the branches. Help Denny avoid them and keep following Glow.
denny_059_answer: Spider silk is very strong for something so thin. Some webs are sticky so insects get caught inside.
denny_059_completion: Denny zigzagged past every web. Glow blinked proudly and led him onward to the last surprise of the night.
denny_060_instruction: A giant leaf path is glowing in the moonlight. Help Denny collect every autumn leaf and follow the curvy trail to Glow.
denny_060_answer: Leaves look green in summer because of chlorophyll. In autumn, the green fades and yellow, orange, and red colors can show.
denny_060_completion: Denny gathered every glowing leaf and reached Glow at the tip of the giant leaf path. The whole forest shimmered softly around them.
denny_061_instruction: Denny hears something rustling in the autumn leaves. Help him follow the path to the leaf pile and find out what it is.
denny_061_answer: Fallen leaves slowly break down into tiny pieces. Worms, fungi, and other small decomposers help turn them into rich soil that feeds trees and new plants.
denny_061_completion: It was only the wind tossing the crunchy leaves into the air. Denny laughed and jumped into the soft golden pile!
denny_062_instruction: The apples rolled away in the wind. Help Denny collect them and bring them back to the basket.
denny_062_answer: An apple floats because about one quarter of it is made of tiny air pockets. Those pockets make the whole apple less dense than water, so it stays at the surface.
denny_062_completion: Denny gathered every apple and tucked them safely into the basket!
denny_063_instruction: Denny hears a whisper in the corn. Help him collect the corn and find the maze exit.
denny_063_answer: Every strand of corn silk connects to one kernel on the cob. Pollen travels down the silk to help that kernel grow, which is why a cob has so many silky threads.
denny_063_completion: The whisper came from the dry corn leaves brushing together. Denny collected the corn and found the gate!
denny_064_instruction: The biggest pumpkin is hiding in the patch. Help Denny collect the little pumpkins and find it.
denny_064_answer: A pumpkin is a fruit because it grows from a flower and contains seeds. Pumpkins belong to the same plant family as cucumbers, melons, and squash.
denny_064_completion: Denny collected the little pumpkins and found the biggest, roundest pumpkin in the patch!
denny_065_instruction: Hazel the squirrel needs acorns for winter. Help Denny collect them and follow the trail to her.
denny_065_answer: Squirrels hide acorns in many small places so they have food during winter. They do not find every hidden acorn, and some forgotten ones can sprout into new oak trees.
denny_065_completion: Denny brought every acorn to Hazel. She tucked them into her hiding places and thanked Denny with a happy little tail wiggle!
denny_066_instruction: The autumn rain is starting. Help Denny avoid the puddles and reach the umbrella.
denny_066_answer: Puddles form when rainwater gathers in low places faster than the ground can soak it up. Sunlight, wind, and warmer air later help the water evaporate.
denny_066_completion: Denny tiptoed around every puddle and reached the umbrella warm and dry!
